clue.text: Tongue of a head briefly restricted by gag

indicators.note: something restricted by a gag is held inside it, so the gag word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a jape is a joke or prank, a gag
taken as written

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word for a headland loses its final letter

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbouring capes

explanation.surface: Someone's tongue is briefly held back by a gag over their mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: JAPE opens to take A plus NES, giving JAP-ANES-E. 'Tongue' looks like the body part but means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue is an old word for a language, and Japanese is the language spoken in Japan.

clue.text: Commentator's curse: wingers that can certainly turn heads!

definitions.text: wingers that can certainly turn heads!

indicators.note: a commentator speaks rather than writes, so we want what the next word sounds like

parts.note: a jinx is a curse bringing bad luck; the bird's name is said the same way

explanation.surface: A football commentator blames a curse on wingers so good they turn spectators' heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wingers' suggests footballers on the flanks; here they are birds. The wryneck, genus Jynx, can twist its head almost right round.
explanation.definitionFit: The wryneck birds are wingers in the flying sense, famous for rotating their necks to an extraordinary degree.

clue.text: US poet transfixed by unknown tree and with it the singular worms

indicators.note: something transfixed by a spike has it run through its middle, so the poet's name is pierced by the next letter

parts.note: Sylvia Plath, the American poet
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
the elm is a common tree
in means fashionable, with it
taken as written
s is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: An American poet is pinned by a tree beside some peculiar worms, a gothic garden scene.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAT-Y-H, then ELM, IN, THE, S: PLATYHELMINTHES. The first 'the' is a link and the second is a piece; 'singular' looks like an adjective for the worms but just gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: Platyhelminthes is the zoological phylum of the flatworms, including tapeworms and flukes.

clue.text: A large measure of intelligence needed to follow mostly awful script

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word for awful drops its last letter
the measure of intelligence is placed to follow, after, the shortened word

parts.note: nasty means awful, very unpleasant
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
IQ, intelligence quotient, is a measure of intelligence

explanation.surface: Deciphering an awful script demands a large amount of brainpower.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is built backwards from the clue's order: the shortened word for awful leads, and the other pieces follow it, as 'to follow' instructs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastaliq is a flowing calligraphic style of Arabic lettering, used mainly for Persian and Urdu writing.

clue.text: Second to first in Atlantic race gives us something to chew on

indicators.note: sending a letter to first means taking it from its spot and putting it at the very front

parts.note: s is the standard abbreviation for second
the Irish, a people living on the edge of the Atlantic

explanation.surface: Coming second in a transatlantic race at least gives the crew something to think about.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of IRISH moves from its fifth place to the front: S-IRIH. 'Atlantic race' sounds like a yacht race but means a people.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirih is the betel leaf, wrapped round areca nut and lime and chewed as a stimulant across South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Huntsman, keeping a beagle (oddly), famously shot Texan

indicators.note: a thing keeping others holds them inside, so the Texan's initials wrap round what follows

parts.note: J.R. Ewing of the TV soap Dallas, whose shooting was a famous cliffhanger
taken as written

indicators.note: oddly here means in the odd manner, discarding the odd-numbered letters so the even ones stay

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of beagle

explanation.surface: A huntsman with a beagle at his side fires on a Texan.
explanation.walkthrough: J(A + EGE)R. 'Oddly' would usually keep the odd letters; here it takes the evens, the opposite of the obvious reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaeger is German for hunter, used in English for a huntsman or rifleman, and also a predatory seabird.

clue.text: Rounding up moose, vehicle seeing off duck and small seabird

indicators.note: rounding means going round something, so the shortened vehicle surrounds the turned beast
seeing off a thing gets rid of it, so the duck symbol is dropped

parts.note: an auto is a car
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the shape of O

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: elk is the European name for the moose

explanation.surface: A driver swerving round a moose kills a duck and a little seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird of the surface but is cricket's score of zero, the shape of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Auklets are the smallest members of the auk family, compact diving birds of northern seas.

clue.text: I beg regional zoo to sort out what's left of marine life

indicators.note: to sort out a muddle is to reorder its parts, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: all fifteen letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A plea to a local zoo to deal with the remains of some sea creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: This ocean-floor sediment is made largely of the chalky shells of dead foraminifera, the remains of tiny marine organisms.

clue.text: Fagged at Gordonstoun: from memory terms, from what we're told, light

parts.note: RAM, random-access memory, a computer's working memory

indicators.note: what we are told is heard rather than seen, so the preceding word is taken by its sound

parts.note: terms of payment are fees; this spelling is said the same way
an LED, light-emitting diode, is a small light

explanation.surface: A worn-out pupil at a Scottish boarding school, with talk of memory, school terms and fees.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordonstoun is a boarding school in Scotland, signalling a Scots word; fagged means exhausted, not a public-school servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramfeezled is a Scots word, used by Burns, meaning worn out or exhausted, which is what fagged means.

clue.text: Call to one's beloved liveried servants

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an affectionate greeting to dear ones, as in the Northern English term of endearment
second meaning: plural of a Hungarian word for a footman in livery, also spelt haiduk

explanation.walkthrough: The two readings are split differently: two words in the greeting, one plural noun for the servants.
explanation.definitionFit: Hey is a greeting and duck is a Northern English endearment; heyducks were also uniformed attendants in Hungarian noble households.

clue.text: Foolishness after returning home, briefly to help unending row

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for home is read the other way

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word for help loses its final letter

parts.note: aid means help

indicators.note: unending means having no end, so the word for row drops its last letter

parts.note: a row of things is a series

explanation.surface: A silly row breaks out after someone comes home to lend a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel but means a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Niaiserie is a French borrowing for silliness or a piece of simple-minded folly.

clue.text: Craft that's departed African city for change turning up in Nouakchott

indicators.note: something that has departed has left, so those letters go missing from the city's name

parts.note: Khartoum is the capital of Sudan
a craft is an art or skill

explanation.surface: A boat has left one African city and is turning up in another to be changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat; it means a skill. Nouakchott is the capital of Mauritania.
explanation.definitionFit: The khoum is a fifth of a Mauritanian ouguiya, so it is small change you might find in that country's capital.

clue.text: Moulding of ace for rugby in Wales

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means swapping it into that place

parts.note: A is the card-game abbreviation for ace
RU stands for Rugby Union
Cymru is the Welsh name for Wales

explanation.surface: A star player, an ace, is shaped into the rugby side of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The RU at the end of CYMRU is replaced by A.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyma is an architectural moulding whose profile is an S-shaped double curve, as in cyma recta.

clue.text: Romantic couple having this gemstone might be just married

parts.note: surface reading: a pair of lovers who own a particular precious stone
setter's reading: split the stone's name and adjust its end and it describes a concealed bond, the state of a couple who have only just wed in secret

explanation.surface: Lovers who own a certain jewel might have just tied the knot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the gem's name as HIDDEN plus TIE with its last letters juggled: a couple with a hidden tie are secretly married.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiddenite is a green variety of the mineral spodumene, cut and set as a precious stone.

clue.text: Relief as Unchained Melody covers number one in Italy and later India

indicators.note: a thing that covers others goes over and around them, so the music term wraps the two letters

parts.note: staccato music has its notes detached, not chained together; Unchained Melody is also a famous song

indicators.note: the number one letter in a word is its very first

parts.note: the opening letter of Italy
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A crooner finds relief singing Unchained Melody first in Italy and then in India.
explanation.walkthrough: The song title is read literally: a melody without chains, its notes disconnected. One I goes in early, the second ('later') further along: ST-I-ACC-I-ATO.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiacciato is a very shallow form of carved relief, famously used by Donatello in Renaissance sculpture.

clue.text: British engineer of note, pally with interior minister

indicators.note: interior means on the inside, so the minister sits inside the musical note

parts.note: ti, or te, is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
Rev is short for Reverend, a minister of religion
to be thick with someone is to be very friendly with them

explanation.surface: A notable British engineer is on friendly terms with the Home Secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interior minister' looks like a government post; 'interior' is really the instruction to place the minister inside the note.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Trevithick, the Cornish engineer, built the first working railway steam locomotive in 1804.

clue.text: Unfasten securing ring lodged in chap's old tree

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so the word for unfasten takes in the ring

parts.note: a chap is a he, a man

indicators.note: a thing lodged in another is stuck within it, so the combination sits inside the chap

parts.note: to unpin is to unfasten
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone releases a ring caught in the bark of a man's ancient tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the ring goes inside the unfastening word just after its first letter, and that whole lot then sits inside the chap.
explanation.definitionFit: The Huon pine of Tasmania is one of the longest-lived trees on Earth, with stands thousands of years old.

clue.text: Romeo leaving place for Sherry's brother

indicators.note: a letter leaving a word departs from it, so it is taken out

parts.note: Jerez in Andalusia is the home of sherry, whose name comes from the town
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo walks out on Sherry's place to visit her brother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sherry' looks like a woman's name; it is the drink. 'Brother!' is the exclamation, not a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise or exasperation, as in 'Oh, brother!'.

clue.text: Bonnie and Clyde's little fat friend's first visits

parts.note: wee is Scots for little

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so this letter enters the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of friend

explanation.surface: The outlaw couple's small, plump friend drops in on them.
explanation.walkthrough: The gangsters are a misdirection: Bonnie is the adjective, and Clyde's means as said on the Clyde, in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Weel-faured is Scots for well-favoured, good-looking, which is what bonnie means.

clue.text: Massage arms supply — ultimate in pain for the first minute

indicators.note: one thing for another means swapped into its place

parts.note: ammo, ammunition, is what arms are supplied with

indicators.note: the ultimate in a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of pain
m is short for minute; the first M of the word is the one replaced

explanation.surface: A massage on the arms supplies a minute of pain at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: AMMO has two Ms; only the first is swapped for N.
explanation.definitionFit: An mo is a traditional Chinese form of therapeutic massage, using pressing and rubbing techniques.

clue.text: Black olives he's cooked turn red

indicators.note: cooked means tampered with, as accounts are cooked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
rearrangement of these nine letters

explanation.surface: Black olives turn red when a chef cooks them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a colour change in cooking; it means communist.
explanation.definitionFit: To Bolshevise is to make Bolshevik, converting a person or state to communism, and red is shorthand for communist.

clue.text: More than one muscle in climbing that is supporting an excessive amount

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporter sits underneath, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: a glut is an excessive supply

indicators.note: climbing goes upward, and in a down clue that means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A climber's muscles hold up against an excessive load.
explanation.definitionFit: Glutei is the Latin plural of gluteus, the buttock muscles, so it is more than one muscle.

clue.text: New pelican crossing not designed originally for one knocked down in alley

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally points to the opening, so each of the two words gives its first letter

parts.note: the opening letters of not and designed

explanation.surface: A brand-new pelican crossing has been built without proper design.
explanation.walkthrough: A pelican crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with push-button lights. 'Alley' is a bowling alley, not a lane.
explanation.definitionFit: A candlepin is a tall thin skittle in candlepin bowling, a variant played in New England; the pins are knocked down by balls.

clue.text: Instances of light above the blessed clouds!

definitions.text: Instances of light above the blessed
definitions.meaning: first meaning: haloes, the glowing rings painted over saints' heads
second meaning: plural of a word for a rain cloud

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are the plural of one Latin word, for a halo and a rain-bearing cloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is both the halo round a holy figure's head and a grey rain cloud, so its plural fits each.

clue.text: Fish caught, topped and turned with the meat served again for feast

indicators.note: serving something again means adding a second helping, so that letter is added on
turned means swung round, so what is left is read the other way
topped means having its top cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a haul is the catch of fish taken in a net
the meat is the central letter of what remains after the turn

explanation.surface: Fish is caught, prepared and turned, then the meat is served again at a big meal.
explanation.walkthrough: HAUL loses its H, AUL turns to LUA, and its middle letter is repeated at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A luau is a Hawaiian party or banquet, traditionally with roast pig and poi.

clue.text: Wheel engineer out of centre to see music event

indicators.note: out of centre means taking the middle away, so the central letters go

parts.note: George Ferris designed the big wheel named after him

explanation.surface: An engineer steps away from the middle of a fairground wheel to watch a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: FERRIS loses its middle pair RR.
explanation.definitionFit: A feis is an Irish or Scottish Gaelic festival of traditional music, song and dance.

clue.text: I see it now, having secured release primarily and enlightenment at last?

definitions.text: I see it now, having secured release primarily and enlightenment at last?

indicators.note: having secured something means holding it firmly inside, so the exclamation wraps the letter

parts.note: aha is the cry of sudden understanding

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of release

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of enlightenment

explanation.surface: A moment of realisation: having gained release, enlightenment arrives at last.
explanation.walkthrough: A(R)HA then T. The whole clue also describes the answer: someone who has achieved release and final enlightenment.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism an arhat is a perfected person who has attained nirvana, released from the cycle of rebirth.

clue.text: Scot's refusal to allow Frenchmen a short vacation in spring near Perth?

indicators.note: to allow in is to admit, so the Scots refusal takes the rest inside it

parts.note: nae is Scots for no
MM is the abbreviation for Messieurs
taken as written
hol is a short form of holiday

explanation.surface: A Scot refuses some Frenchmen a quick spring break near Perth.
explanation.walkthrough: NA(MM A HOL)E. 'Perth' with 'Scot' in the clue suggests Scotland, but this Perth is in Western Australia, and 'spring' is a water source, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnamma or namma hole is a natural rock waterhole in the Western Australian desert, a source of water like a spring.

clue.text: Essential for eg backbone of some companies: solid backing

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the found letters are read right to left
some means only part of what follows, so the letters are found within the words

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Solid financial backing is the backbone of some companies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backbone' sounds like business talk but is literal: the spine is bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossein is the collagen-based organic matrix of bone, so it is an essential component of the spine.

clue.text: Old market traders, increasingly treacherous, heading to the East End

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and sending it to the end means moving it to the back

parts.note: skiddier means more slippery, as a treacherous road becomes

explanation.surface: Old costermongers grow ever more untrustworthy as they head for London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treacherous' suggests betrayal; here it means slippery underfoot. The East End is the traditional home of London market traders, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiddier is an obsolete word for a huckster or travelling dealer who bought goods to sell at market.
